chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: The Jade Room double booking with Kid Ory
summary: Booked into the same club as Kid Ory, McGhee's modern band is resented and let go after three weeks.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Then I went into this club where Kid Ory was working...
What was that, the Jade...
The Jade Room, right. Boy, they hated me in that room! Ha-ha!
What do you mean? They had the two bands at once?
They had two bands at once.
How did they happen to make a booking like that?

Well, the agent didn't know what they were playing, and he didn't know what I was playing -- because he had never been to hear me play, you know. But anyway, he booked me into this club. And Kid Ory hit the ceiling, you know. Because he didn't have the type of band that... I had an entertaining band with a lot of flash, and a lot of fast tunes and so forth and so on, and what they had was the old traditional things that they did way back yonder, you know. The people, they didn't know the difference; they couldn't tell what was going on. They liked me as well as they did him, but Kid Ory didn't like that -- he didn't want nobody to be in there with him, you know.
So the guy said, 'Well, Howard, I'm going to have to let you go, because we've got a conflict here between what's happening.' And I said, 'Okay, well, if that's the way it is, that's the way it is.'
Did Kid Ory ever say anything to you personally?

Well, he let know he didn't like me. He wouldn't say nothin' to me, you know what I mean. Like I said, 'Now we're going to bring on the wonderful Kid Ory' and all this shit, but what he said was 'Now we're going to bring on the Howard McGhee band,' and that's all he said. I said, 'Okay, all right.' But I mean, that's the way it was in those days, man.
Well, in those days there was two camps.
That's right.
As they called them in the magazines, "the moldy figs" and "the beboppers." And there was no...
No in-between. There was no in-between.
It was very bitter.
Yeah. They thought we were out there trying to take their job. And I didn't give a goddamn about their job or anybody else's job. I was just trying to play my horn.
Oh boy, though, man... We had trouble at the Jade Room.
How long were you at the Jade Room?

We were there a little over three weeks. Then the guy said, well, he had to let us go because Kid was going around telling the customers to get up and leave when we'd come on. "You don't want to listen to that. Get up and leave..." But he was pulling against me. I didn't care whether he was pulling against me anyway, because it was only a job. But to Kid Ory, it was his haven. You know, that was...
That was his place.
